priorCorrection.previous: Three survivors plus an ideal excluded full bridge hard-bond N=M were described as an exhaustive topology cut.
priorCorrection.now: The source phrases allow cap/coil diode-OR input groups and finite-impedance N-M links. CT/bridge/split-rail are not exhaustive; split-rail is a distinct load/reference assignment on a bridge skeleton rather than an independent four-diode orientation graph. Ideal bridge N=M is incompatible with an independently held nonzero ideal source voltage, but with finite source impedance it creates a real, energy-consuming winding clamp path rather than a logical impossibility.
priorCorrection.physicalConclusion: Physical operation not established or ruled out; actual current depends on transformer winding impedances, diode direction, return impedance, phase, switching and power sources.

selectedHypotheses: A-M=+v and B-M=-v in ideal symmetric unloaded source
source impedances finite Rs>0 in nonideal loop comparison
ideal diode paths oriented N->negative outer winding for conventional bridge
resistive load RL>0 at separate positive branch

derivedElectricalModel.idealSourceNoGo: N=M imposes 0=V_N-V_M whereas an otherwise unperturbed conventional bridge imposes V_N-V_M=-abs(v), contradictory at abs(v)>0.

nonidealHardBond.pathEachHalfCycle: M=N -> conventional bridge return diode -> currently negative end (B if A positive, A if B positive) -> source winding and internal series impedance -> M
nonidealHardBond.clampCurrent: I_clamp=abs(v)/Rs for zero-drop diode and independent half-winding Thevenin model

normalizedExample.units: arbitrary normalized units, not a Filsinger observation

nonidealHardBond.qualification: Actual transformer halves are coupled and diode drops, saturation, core loss and parasitics alter the formula. Not a safe build suggestion.

derivedElectricalModel.resistorMediated: When N is coupled to M by finite resistance Rb, current abs(v)/(Rs+Rb); N-M=-abs(v)*Rb/(Rs+Rb); real source costs include losses in both resistances.
derivedElectricalModel.capacitorMediated: At sinusoidal RMS V with series Rs and return capacitance C, I=V/(Rs+1/(i omega C)); Psource=Rs*abs(I)^2 and ideal cap average P=0. Low-frequency no path, high-frequency approaches short; can rotate current phase without an external generator.
derivedElectricalModel.coilCapResonantMediated: Z=Rs+i(omega L-1/(omega C)); at resonance reactive terms cancel and source current = V/Rs; finite source losses still paid. Original coil/cap phase claim is a mechanism hypothesis, not physically identified values.
derivedElectricalModel.diodeOrCapCoilGroup: Two packages from capacitor-coupled wire X and two from coil wire Y, each oriented X/Y->P and ganged cathodes, can diode-OR their respective branch potentials. This would be two effective positive rectifying paths, not proof of two independently replenished donors. If X/Y are actually the same node by wiring, their independence disappears.
